Cord, 510 Joules, 2 USB Charging Ports, Black, $20K Insurance & (TLP310USBC) When you own and use many electronics, you need a place to plug them in- something that goes far beyond the standard 2 plug wall socket. A surge strip is ideal because it not only serves as an extension cord, it also helps protect valuable electronics from harm. And a good tool for the task is Tripp Lite 6 Outlet Desk Clamp Surge Protector Power Strip.

With this power strip, you get six traditional style outlets and two USB ports, perfect for charging your cell phones. There is an on/off switch and an indicator light that confirms the surge protection is working. This latter feature is one you don’t normally see with other power strips and it provides added peace of mind.

This power strip is u- shaped and comes with a clamp so it can be attached to a desk. The clamp won’t work on just any desk, as I learned, because some desks are too thin. You need a thick spot to clamp. And keep in mind that the clamp isn’t super strong. It can still slip a little but this shouldn’t be an issue in most instances.

UL listed and with a long cord, the Tripp Lite 6 Outlet Desk Clamp Surge Protector Power Strip is practical and useful for most home office needs. Mine has already been put to use in my office, as you can see in the picture, providing a place for my wife to plug in all of her electronics and keep them safe from surges. It’s a useful device that makes a good addition to any home.

Slim & Expandable Laptop Backpack 15 15.6 16 Inch Sleeve with USB Port, Spill-Resistant Notebooks Bag Case for Most 14-16 Inch MacBooks Surface-Books Dell HP Lenovo Asus Computers, Pure Black I see this as a vertical laptop sleeve with the option to carry it like a back pack.

I like that the back pack straps tuck away so flatly and completely that it looks like a sleeve and doesn't look or feel clunky. You won't notice the straps until you decide to use them. There is also a strap for sliding over luggage handle.

It fits my 14" laptop with a little room left over. When kept as a sleeve (and not opened into the bigger bag option), I can tuck my mouse and charging cord in with the lap top.

The interior is soft and padded and is about what I expect from a sleeve, maybe even more secure. No issues.

There are two front zipper pockets while it is in the sleeve configuration.

An option to unzip a compartment that makes it into a bigger bag (or backpack) then provides even more space and storage options. Including two mesh side pockets for water bottles or whatever. Additional storage isn't significant, but it is functional. Can easily be used as a day bag (pack some snacks, and few other essentials), maybe pushing it as an overnight bag (unless super minimalist), but it is definitely great as a sleeve that can be opened up to carry more treasures. Doubt I would have used this as my high school or college pack pack because I usually carried a lot, and I dont think this will carry much more than a book or two. It simply isn't a traditional back pack, but I dont think you would be looking at this if that is what you were after.

The material has a smooth canvas feel. Very clean lines. Minimalist look. I have this in wine red, and it a great color.

I like it, and it is much nicer, sturdier, and attractive than I expected.

Unless it falls apart on me soon, I see no reason not to give it full rating. If I experience anything else, I will be back to update.

"Slim & Expandable Design: Slim style for light travel and commute, 200% Expandability when more belongings and easily to switch between the both."

However, after my family kept telling her how great it was and how much she would love it, she finally agreed to give it a try. A few months after we purchased her first kindle, it broke and Amazon sent her another one, but that kindle also broke and Amazon is refusing to replace it.

Not only has Amazon ruined her experience/impression on using tablets, but the refusal to repair the charging component so many other customers have experienced problems with is unacceptable. I am a frequent shopper of Amazon, but after hearing that my mother's second kindle is not working and Amazon has refused to replace or repair it has made me reconsider my shopping preferences. My mother no longer wants to even use the kindle, she told me not to "worry about getting it fixed" because it's been such a hassle; which is disappointing considering how much my family lobbied for the product promising her that she would love how much it would improve her life.

Otium Bluetooth Headphones, Wireless Headphones IPX7 Waterproof Sports Earbuds 15H Playtime with Mic HD Stereo Sound Sweatproof in-Ear Earphoones Noise Cancelling Headsets Gym Running Workout Pink My Otium beats will be four years old in July. I've tried to upgrade earbuds (nothing too pricey) and have always been disappointed.

🏋🏼‍♀️ I wear them while I work out. They have a great sound and block outside noise pretty well. They help me get in my zone in my own little world, and I love them.

💦 I tried to swim in them, and while they're waterproof, they stop playing as soon as my head is underwater.

🎧 The plastic ear tips, which are super comfortable for my tiny ear holes, eventually broke down — as aging plastic will do. I replaced them with BLLQ Replacement Ear Tips, which are nearly identical to the originals [[ASIN:B07FF9DN5K BLLQ Replacement Ear Tips]].

💵 They're $20. BT 4.1. So not the newest Bluetooth, and I'm sure Bose sounds better. But at this price point, I love these little guys.

🏆 Actually, I got them on a lightning sale for $13, so even better! So I paid $20 for the earbuds AND replacement tips.

🌚 I still want something new because I just want something new, you know. But knowing the disappointment I always feel with my attempted replacements, I'll probably keep using these sweet little babies.

🔊 I don't know what the heck they're talking about with the "noise canceling" in the product title. There is no ACTIVE noise-canceling, but the earbuds do form slight seals, which have a passive noise-canceling effect. I think I actually bought them for noise-canceling, but whatever. It's overrated as a feature unless you are willing to pay hundreds of dollars.

In sum, these are great earbuds, especially if you're prone to losing things and hate to feel heartbroken about losing something expensive.
text_fidelity_b: Otium Bluetooth Headphones, Wireless Headphones IPX7 Waterproof Sports Earbuds 15H Playtime with Mic HD Stereo Sound Sweatproof in-Ear Earphoones Noise Cancelling Headsets Gym Running Workout Pink

Microsoft Surface Book 13.5" (Intel Core i5, 8GB RAM, 256 GB) So my only complaint about Microsoft devices as a whole is their lack of compatibility with Linux. This one is better than the other 4 I have owned. It still isn't working well with CentOS, but Kubuntu works awesomely, and I also have Kali running. I've got a tripple boot (with Windows as well) set up, and the whole thing took about 5 hours to set up. If you're looking for a laptop to run Linux on, that is light and has a great battery, the choice is this one or the XPS. The XPS (my friend has one) doesn't run touchscreen, but it is lighter than this one and gets even better battery...

Overall, this laptop has a great battery, a great screen, and runs Linux with very little effort. The only downsides are the requirement to have power connected in order to detach the screen (yes, the button does work in Linux), the fact that all ports (USB, SD and charging included) are on the base (so in tablet mode it can't charge, can't read an SD card, and can't use a USB device), and the fact that it is so sealed that you can't upgrade or repair it yourself. Those are the reasons I dropped one star (personally, I'd drop 4 stars for all that, but I know most people wouldn't).

As a matter of fact, I couldn't connect to it at all. So right off the bat, that is something to note... that paying more for a camera doesn't necessarily mean better wi-fi receivers are inside the camera. This isn't something I'm going to subtract a star for since no cameras on the market can help with my wi-fi situation, that's something that will have to be remedied by wi-fi extenders.

Now once I move this camera indoor, with better wi-fi reception, to monitor the backyard, it does the job wonderfully! The app is great and full of features. Be sure you select the proper MODE. By default, it was on BASIC and it did not do any recordings. I realize I had to change it to PROTECTION mode or 24/7 mode. Or, better yet, you can create your own mode! You can determine if it will record 24/7, or only when it detects motion. You can determine the duration of the clip. Now that is pretty cool! The default is 10 seconds, and for several weeks I thought I had to live with the default, until I discovered that I can actually change this by creating my own Mode. You can determine if it will notify you for every motion detected, or only for human detections. Lastly, you can name the mode anything you want, then select it and you're set! I've only used Wyze, Arlo and Homehawk cameras, and without a doubt, this Panasonic software is the best of the bunch. 5-stars!

Ecolink Intelligent Technology Z-Wave Pet Immunity Motion Detector with Pet Immunity, White (PIRZWAVE2-ECO) I was hopeful for this product given some of the positive reviews. We're using this in our kitchen to turn on sofit and undercounter lighting when anyone walks in (very cool, btw). We used X10 for years without a problem but really wanted to integrate this into our new SmartHub/Things setup.

Installing any Ecolink product is a little frustrating since the instructions are merely: plug it in and follow your controller manufacturer's instructions for adding a device. Well, the SmartThings hub is brilliant but it takes awhile for any Ecolink device to be found and I usually have to unplug and re-plug them in several times to get it to work. This, however, is simply a BATTERY OPERATED stand-alone device so it's a bit more cryptic so had to pop the battery out a few times to get it to work. I finally got it working after replacing battery with a fresh one. The battery it shipped with was dead.

Behavior. I set this up to turn on the lights and then off when there is no movement. We expected this sensor to have PIR (ON while motion is in the room). Well it does not PIR so it keeps turning the light off at the end of the timer whether there is motion or not. The sensor simply does not sense again for about 5-10 minutes after the original movement. Not sure how to figure that out. We're going to try to figure it out but without knowing what kind of sensor this is we're probably going to return it or trash it.

text_fidelity_a: SAMSUNG 34-Inch Odyssey G85SB Series QD-OLED Ultra WQHD Curved Gaming Monitor, 175Hz, 0.03ms, DisplayHDR True Black 400, AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, Advanced Game Streaming, LS34BG850SNXZA, 2023 Putting together this beast was not a very difficult task.  I am using the 'Ergotron – HX Single Ultrawide Monitor Arm' with this monitor.  There was a little bit of an odd feeling when it took me hooking both hdmi and display port up to figure out how to deal with the monitor source correctly.  This overall though is the most amazing monitor I've ever sat in front of.  I use this for engineering work as I'm not a gamer.  The screen real estate is much larger than typical 4k 1440p monitors.  The jump from a 34" to 49" was not as drastic of an impression as I would have expected.  The curve softens the hit to the senses as it seems a little shorter than it actually is.  The curve takes a little getting used to but it's not near as aggressive as people claim.  This is my first curved monitor because I didn't know if I could get used to it or not.  After a few hours of working on it, I barely notice anymore.  The picture is very clean and crisp.  I'm using it in conjunction with a sapphire card.  There are plenty of reviews about the exact specs of this monitor, but really I wanted to note that it shines when it comes to just immersing someone into the screen.  I only would suggest this to people that have a very deep measuring desk because this does take up quite a lot of room over the desk even with an arm holding it up.  Works well with Ubuntu 22.04 + Gnome + Wayland using a Sapphire Radeon Pulse RX 5600 XT which does PCIE 4.0 and has for a long time now.  The card actually handles it very easily at 120hz on gnome for daily grinds, fans are not even moving at the moment.  The booklet instructions are confusing, so while waiting for the monitor to ship I would suggest watching some unboxing.

text_fidelity_a:
StarTech.com Dual Monitor USB 3.0 Laptop Docking Station with HDMI & DVI/VGA, 6x USB-A Hub, GbE, Audio, Universal Type-A Dock - Windows/macOS/ChromeOS (USB3SDOCKHD) I had high hopes for this docking station from StarTech but, thus far, I’ve been pretty disappointed.

Like many people I like the portability of working from a laptop but when I am at my workstation I want more screen space to work on - I thought this Docking Station would be a perfect solution. Well, in theory, it would.

Inside the box you’ll find the docking station, a 3.0 USB cable, a power adapter with snap on plugs to fit various world power sources, a DVI to VGA adapter, and a CD-ROM.

Unlike many docking stations or hubs this is not Plug and Play. I’m running the most updated Windows 10 64bit and the CD-ROM is completely useless. After inserting it in my computer I received a message reading that it was not compatible with my machine. No problem, I went to the manufacturer’s website, found the product, clicked on support, downloaded the zip file containing the setup and updated drivers for my OS and continued.

I went through the installation process and it appeared to install fine. After accepting the user agreement it checked my system for compatibility - finding no issues it continued and completed installation. I went to device manager and noticed an error in USB connected devices but figured with a restart it would correct.

I restarted but the error remains. Configuration Descriptor Request Failed - Windows has stopped device. I have uninstalled and reinstalled, searched help, used Windows Update to search for a better driver - so far nothing has worked.

In regards to functionality - the USB ports (two 3.0 and four 2.0) all function without issue and the Ethernet Port works great providing me over 200Mb/s. Due to not having the correct drivers I’ve been unable to test the multiple monitor capabilities.

I have contacted tech support and as of writing I have not heard back. If they are able to help me solve these issues I will update my review to reflect my further findings.

It appears this Docking Station is outdated being developed for older operating systems and while it may work for some users, others will find it needlessly difficult.

I would look at more recently manufactured docking stations that have been developed with the current operating systems - especially if you are using Windows 10.
text_fidelity_b: StarTech.com Dual Monitor USB 3.0 Laptop Docking Station with HDMI & DVI/VGA, 6x USB-A Hub, GbE, Audio, Universal Type-A Dock - Windows/macOS/ChromeOS (USB3SDOCKHD)

text_fidelity_a:
Bose Conversation Enhancing Headphones Black (770341-0010) I’m 40 and have high frequency hearing loss. I hear almost nothing from 1kHz & up in my right ear and 4kHz and up in my left ear. I only experience issues in loud environments(restaurants, etc) or when there is a lot of background noise, but I recently started experiencing low frequency tinnitus that was irritating so I started looking for solutions. I went to see an ENT doctor and went through the motions only for him to confirm that I have poor hearing for my age and it’s up to me if I want some expensive hearing aids. No way I’m dropping 5k... I began by just looking for something to relieve the tinnitus and ran across many people saying that noise canceling headphones helped. I then went to the Bose website and low and behold they had the Hearphones which also had noise canceling. I started reading reviews then first then I stopped by the store with my kids and tried them out. My son was across the store and I could hear him talking to his sister. I could also hear every word of the conversation of people not far away. I removed the Hearphones and could not hear my kids or the people talking. I did this a few times... tuning in on people, music, etc then removing the buds. Tried the noise canceling and the rumbling in my ears was almost gone. Needless to say, I was impressed. I discussed the warranty with the salesman...30 day return, 90 exchange for something else, & 1 year free replacement(btw the 1 yr starts replacement over every time you replace them). I was sold. I purchased them with the intention of using for 30 days and returning if I could do without them.

I have now had them for 1 month. Here is my experience... at first I hated the neckband and was considering returning, but I got used to it and now don’t notice it. I use them for 1 hour workouts every morning, driving in the car for phone calls, music, podcasts, noise canceling at work, so pretty much all day. The neckband twists a little while working out or running and you need to shift it back in place, but it’s not a big deal for me. I would prefer the Soundsport Frees for working out, but I can’t bring myself to spend another $200 for headphones when these are $500. The noise canceling is fantastic for the gym & office and allows me to listen to music at a much lower level, which saves what I have left of my hearing in the long run. I used the soundsport wireless for 1 year before getting these and the sound quality of the hearphones is better, plus the noise canceling, and it has the music boost/phone call boost. I gave my soundsports to my wife and now use these exclusively.

Hearing:
When there is a lot of noise I can put them on and hear every word of a conversation that I would normally not hear or tune all the noise out via the noise cancellation. I recently went to a concert and was shocked at how much I enjoyed the concert more while wearing them. I could hear the guitar strings, vocals, and so much more while having a conversation with my wife. Amazing! I even use them while listening to the stereo in my car because it sounds so much better. I am always surprised at the sounds that I miss while not wearing them.

Sound: Classic Bose sound. The best headphones I’ve owned and I’ve had a few nice sets including the Bose soundsports & Bowers & Wilkins. I enjoy music much more since having them.

Phone calls: Phone calls are so much better, I talk on the phone more now because I’m not struggling to hear the other person and I hear them in both ears.

Overall: They simply work great. One of the best features is the directivity. When you set it to front or focused it ignores the rear microphones. While at the same time merging the left & right sound together. You hear a little of the left in the right ear and vice verse which helps with conversations. If Bose can ever put this technology in earbuds like the Frees they probably could not keep them on the shelf. If you have hearing loss or tinnitus and love music buy the Hearphones. If you love music and have no hearing loss buy the QC30 or QC35 for the noise canceling feature.

There are other fun Easter eggs that I didn’t expect...Wearing these while listening to music creates a “karaoke” effect and you can adjust the world volume so that it increases your voice to blend with the music coming through the headphones. I also played my guitar and found that more enjoyable. I could hear the notes in more detail as well as hear my voice in more detail while playing. These are also great if you like to people watch. When you are in a mall or restaurant you can hear random people’s conversations from across the room in detail, while they think you are wearing headphones and not listening at all. If you have hearing loss and/or enjoy a premium set of headphones these are for you. I have not used any other hearing devices to compare, but there are plenty of other reviews that will provide that information.

My rating is 5 stars from my perspective, but here is the breakdown of positives and negatives as I see them:

Positives:
- The sound is amazing for music, podcasts, phone calls, everything. Probably the best sounding headphones next to the QC35
- Adjustable balance. I set the balance to about 20 toward my right ear and both ears feel equal again.
- The adjustable world volume is awesome. I constantly adjust when my surrounding are too loud or not loud enough.
- Treble/bass adjustment. I set the treble around 30 and my world comes to life.
- Noise canceling is superb. It has almost stopped my tinnitus altogether. Especially good in situations like moving the yard. Before the noise of the mower was exhausting , but now it does not bother me.
- Adjustable presets are nice
- The front, focus, & everywhere settings work great. I use the front 180 setting the most. The focus setting really boost voice in front of you which is very nice too.
- Hearing the outside world while listening to music is amazing. Especially when you want to hear music, but want to hear when someone talks to you.
- “Karaoke effect” is pretty cool and makes singing/playing more enjoyable.
Negatives:
- The neckband was annoying at first, but now I barely notice it.
- Sometimes the app does not connect right away, but it connects after a few seconds.
- You will get weird looks from people, but the look is them wandering if you are listening to them since you are wearing headphones. It disappears after you start taking to people.
- I worry about the durability of them sometimes, but with a free replacement of 1 year I feel better about that. Remember that if you swap them with the year the warranty starts over. I am considering the extended warranty they lasts 3 years.
- I don’t like the charge port, but the only thing to improve it would be wireless charging.
- You’ll get wind noise outside. Use the noise canceling.

Btw I bought these in the Bose store and wrote this review to help others with similar issues. The headphones have improved my life and I love using them for just about everything.
text_fidelity_b: Bose Conversation Enhancing Headphones Black (770341-0010)

HP 8100 Desktop Computer Intel i5 3.2GHz Processor 8GB Memory 1TB HDD Genuine Windows 10 Professional (Renewed) I wanted to wait and use it a while before leaving a review.

First off, it is larger than I expected it to be. That's okay - just had to rearrange everything.
Secondly, it is a refurb, so there are limits as to what to expect. My old computer had a hard drive die.
I got a new hard drive, but for some reason, it would never connect to the internet again after that.
I downloaded new drivers, etc etc, but nothing. So, couldn't really go without any longer, so looked for a refurb.

I like sticking with HP because I've used them for years. I've even had refurbs.
This one is different.
First of all, it lays horizontally instead of like the towers I've always had.
It looks a little rough, but not unreasonable.

it grunts at me while using it, much like my old dying hard drive did, so that does worry me a little bit.
It sounds like a grumpy old man who doesn't want to get out of his chair to reach the remote.
There are plenty of USB ports on this one. It lacks some things I'd like to have, but hey...

My biggest complaint is the lack of RAM memory on this. It only came with a measly 8GB.
That might sound okay, but it isn't. Everything moves in slow-motion. Copying files is a nightmare.
I can't afford to buy more memory right now, so I have to just suck it up.
We raided a couple of my other computers which are all HP, but of course, NONE of the six memory sticks I had
will fit this one. *bang head on desk*
The speakers are HORRIBLE. If you have ears, you'll want to replace them or add your own.
I do have speakers, but have not yet hooked them up, because it has to be done on the back, and I have to move
a lot of stuff to pull it back out enough.

This also has Win10, which I dislike a great deal. Seems like everything was moved to a new place just because they could.
But I'll deal with that. Most of the time, I can ignore the Win10 junk.

Overall, it will do what I hired it for, which was to get me back on the internet.
But if you work with graphics (like I do), know that the lack of memory will be sand in your shorts.
Everything takes much longer than on my old HP tower.
text_fidelity_b: HP 8100 Desktop Computer Intel i5 3.2GHz Processor 8GB Memory 1TB HDD Genuine Windows 10 Professional (Renewed)

TRENDnet Wireless AC1750 Dual Band Gigabit Router with USB 3.0 Share Port, Pre-Encrypted, TEW-812DRU Let me preface this review by explaining that I work in the IT industry and support a variety of businesses with enough thorough experience in networking to say with certainty - the router I received is absolute garbage.

Now, normally I'd say for this price that you should set you expectations quite low - being in the field I'm in, I understand that almost all consumer routers are not great options, and the ones that are somewhat viable are on the $300+ range. Not everybody has the money or cares enough to invest this much - I get that.

So, that leaves me and my old roommate pretty much one option; the TRENDnet Wireless AC1750. He doesn't need much and especially doesn't want to spend much, it was tough getting him to go high enough in price to even this router- the old router he had came with his cable subscription 3 years ago. It worked fine but was sometimes slow with downloading over WiFi, not surprising. From the research and reviews, and most importantly the price - we decided to try this Trendnet AC1750 router.

WOW what garbage - he no longer gets WiFi in his bathroom corner of the house - it is a VERY small 2 bedroom apartment. How in the world can this router not handle a signal from 20 feet away, with only 2 walls in between? A router of this caliber (even at this price) should EASILY be able to handle covering a 2 bedroom small apartment. Period.

On to the second problem - even if we're connected, the WiFi signal drops constantly, I have to now reset this router every single day by unplugging it and plugging it back in because it refuses to work longer than 16 hours before crapping out. I have tried updating firmware, all network resets I can. I've even tried using the old modem (we replaced both router + modem) to see if that was the root of our problems - nope, it's the router.

It has slowly been getting worse and worse, and when I am gone from this apartment my roommate will be forced to reset his router every day, sometimes twice a day, just to get internet - or purchase a new one.

I am extremely dissatisfied with this product, although not quite surprised or disappointed given its price. It just seems odd that a 3 year old Netgear N300 router performs much better than an AC1750 Dual Band router.
text_fidelity_b: TRENDnet Wireless AC1750 Dual Band Gigabit Router with USB 3.0 Share Port, Pre-Encrypted, TEW-812DRU

WiFi Wireless Outdoor Security Camera Solar Powered, 1080P Color Night Vision, Motion Detection, Two-Way Audio, Support Google Home and Alexa, Cloud/Local Storage with 64GB TF Card This Wireless WiFi Outdoor Security Camera Solar Battery Powered is a good camera. Taking it out of the box, I was able to tell that it is well-built and well thought out. The solar panel is of good quality and can be mounted on the camera or separately. The necessary USB extension cable and extra mounting arm is included in this camera kit if you decide to mount the panel separately from the camera. Mounting is easy. Just two screws into the eaves and you're done. No wires to pull and no batteries to change. Compare this with systems like Arlo where you would need to break out your ladder to switch out batteries every month or spend extra to purchase a solar panel for each camera.

This camera has all of the standard functions of live feed, motion detection, and night vision but of course it also has the pan and tilt function which helps to get a clearer picture of what you're trying to see. Local SD card storage means that a subscription service isn't necessary to review past events. It's all quite nice. I did find that there is a significant lag in the camera. It can take a full second for any pan and tilt commands to actually go through.

This camera works with the Tuya app (also works with Smart Life) so it's up to you to decide how much you can trust those apps, but otherwise the camera is a solid purchase.

text_fidelity_a:
OP/TECH USA Soft Pouch Digital D-Pro (Black) I bought this cover and the Zing Pro Zoom cover. I like the Op Tech D Pro Zoom better.
Pros:
It was easier to get on and off my camera then the Zing.
It fits my camera and accessories nicely.
Seems well made. I have many other Op Tech products that I purchased and they have all held up nicely.
Cons:
To securely close the cover, there is a flap that has 2 snaps. You wrap the cover around the back of the camera, and snap the flap closed with the 2 snaps. I'm not a fan of snaps. These were easy to snap closed, but Velcro would have been much easier.
There is a strap attached to the inside of the cover. It came with 2 ways of attaching the cover to your camera so you don't lose the cover:
1. a piece of leather that attaches to the camera by screwing it into the tripod mount. This piece attaches to the strap with a snap. I could see either end of the leather coming apart - the side with screw could detach or the snap could release.
2. A ring that can go around the lens. This ring attaches to the strap with a snap. I don't like having things attached to my lens and the snap could release.
I came up with my own method of securing the cover to my camera. The bottom of my battery grip has a connection point for a strap. I had an extra set of Op Tech Uni Loop connectors (https://www.amazon.com/OP-TECH-USA-1301062-Uni-Loop/dp/B0010HA6A6/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1485137755&sr=8-1&keywords=optech+uni+loop).
I attached one end to the bottom of the battery grip. I attached the other connector to the strap by looping the strap thru the connector loop and snapping the two snaps on the strap together. Using the uni loop connectors, I clicked the two pieces together. I think the weakest point is where the snaps are attached. I'm going to sew a few stitches next to the strap as a precaution in case the snaps come undone. You can use any type of strap to secure the cover to the camera. I also attached a photo using an extra camera strap from one of my point and shoot cameras. If I used this method, I would still sew a few stitches next to the snap. I like the uni loop method. If the cover gets in the way, I can just disconnect the uni loop clips.
I'm happy with this cover even though I'm using a different method of attaching the cover to my camera. I dropped the rating to a 4 because of the use of the snaps.
text_fidelity_b: OP/TECH USA Soft Pouch Digital D-Pro (Black)

Amazon Basics 6 Outlet, Wall Mount Surge Protector, Power Strip, 2 USB ports 3.4A, 1080 Joules This AMAZONBASICS 6-OUTLET WALL MOUNT SURGE PROTECTOR (with 2 USB ports 3.4A, 1080 Joules) installs easily--all you need is a screwdriver (flat or Phillips). The surge protector is rated 1080 joules, which is much more protection than you get from most inexpensive surge protectors. This is plenty of protection for the power surges that happen when the power goes out and is restored suddenly.

Because my power company (PGE) delivers a LOT of unexpected power outages, I need surge protectors on all household outlets that service expensive-to-replace electronic equipment (e.g., microwave oven, coffeepot, TV, toaster).

This wall mount surge protector works well in my kitchen, where I have several small appliances that I like to leave plugged in. It also expands a standard 2-outlet wall outlet to 6 outlets. (This is okay, because I don’t plug kitchen appliances into all 6 outlets at once.) The surge protector has an orange light that tells you it is working. If the orange light goes out (for example, after a sudden power outage), then the surge protector needs to be replaced.

The two USB charging outlets are nice to have, but I don’t need them in my kitchen. If you don’t need these, you can buy a cheaper AmazonBasics model that is the same except that it omits the USB feature.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics 6 Outlet, Wall Mount Surge Protector, Power Strip, 2 USB ports 3.4A, 1080 Joules

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Wireless Desktop MK 300 This is the first Logitech keyboard I've gotten, and now I see why Logitech is considered to be a proficient manufacturer in keyboards and other computer-related paraphernalia.

Without installing any such programs or software, either from the website or from the included disc, I plugged in the USB receiver right out of the box, followed the easy-to-setup instructions engraved on the back of the keyboard, and away I went. I was able to type flawlessly at the office, and the keys are very smooth and quiet. Even though it's just a keyboard, I kept opening up different programs to test out the typing. Pure joy! (For a nerd like me, at least.)

I guess the only gripes I have, and I noticed it almost immediately, is that there are no lights to indicate locks for the numbers, caps, or scroll. It's a minor gripe, but a gripe nonetheless since I have to utilize the Caps Lock every so often at work.

When I used the extra buttons for various computer software, I found that the respected programs opened up right away. There was some stall, but that was the result of my slow, crunching computer.
The mouse worked just as it should.

Now, I have to admit, what I really wanted to get this keyboard for was my Wii at home. I know, it sounds nerdy.
But the keyboard I was using before was an old office wired one that was given to me. That one worked fine, but I wanted a wireless one. So, I took home this MK300 keyboard and USB receiver, plugged in the latter into the back of my Wii console, opened up the Internet Channel and found, to my delight, that the keyboard worked flawlessly.
There was some range betwixt the keyboard and receiver--about ten feet or so--but it made no matter: my sitting spot isn't too far from the console, so it's not like I'm going to be typing in a completely different room.

Since this keyboard works so well, I was hoping to use it on a Mac. I've yet to buy the MacBook Pro--which is why I'm stuck with the Wii's Internet Channel for now--and since the specifications for this certain keyboard doesn't include Apple's OS, I'm assuming that there is simply no way around hardware setups (ever tried?) and will have to resort to something else, when the time comes.

All in all, though, if you're looking for an excellent wireless (not Bluetooth) keyboard at a relatively inexpensive price tag for any PC machine or Wii, look no further. The MK300 works like a charm.

2. I noted the 400 was much larger than my old e-trex and seemed "clunkier".

3. However, the biggest frustration was attemping to link the 400 with my boat's navigation program on my laptop. I simply wasn't able to link and their website help page was close to worthless. Never was able to link. My e-trex links right away.

5. Finally, it was discouraging to google "Triton 400" and find so many negative comments about the unit and Magellan's support.

For land use, other than the short battery life, it might present a decent option. But for marine use, I'll stick with my Garmin e-trex.

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech 910000153 V220 Cordless Optical Mouse for Notebooks [[VIDEOID:c6148faf689d084cd73b4a5362755ed1]] Just playing around with my first ever video review, so please bear with me.

The V220 is a pretty good mouse considering the price tag. It's compact and rugged looking, with rubber pads at the sides for a good grip.

It only needs one AA battery (Note: the diagram is misleading with regard to the way to put in the battery. You should see the + side when you're closing the top)

You can use it for desktops as well as laptops.

There's storage space for the receiver at the bottom, and once you click it into place, the mouse automatically shuts off.

The ridged rubber wheel is the noisy variety, and goes click, click, click, all the way home.

It comes with no software, but gives you a link to the website where you can get a download to make the mouse do tricks. After the download, you can scroll from side to side, click and roll to zoom, and if you give it a shove, it can even roll over and play dead.

It has a warning light to tell you when your battery needs changing.

It doesn't come with a case or pouch, but looks like it can handle going commando just fine.

In summary, it's a good mouse, but not a great mouse - and well worth the price.

Amanda Richards, October 9, 2007
text_fidelity_b: Logitech 910000153 V220 Cordless Optical Mouse for Notebooks

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire AIO Touch Desktop, 23.8" Full HD Touch, Intel Core i5-7400T, 12GB DDR4, 1TB HDD, Windows 10 Home, AZ3-715-ACKi5 Computers are an important part of life. I know, I know- we need to get away from electronics and try to return to the days when more personal interactions were the norm. But regardless of how you feel about the proliferation of electronics in everyday living, there is no denying that most of us need them to one degree or another. We are writers/bloggers in my home and need good machines to carry us through the day. And the Acer Aspire Touch Desktop is one excellent machine for everyday use.

Let’s start with the physical attributes. This Acer computer features a very large flat screen with excellent clarity, making it ideal for watching videos, television shows, etc. The keyboard and mouse are wireless, so there is no issue over wires getting tangled as you work. Best of all, the CPU is part of the monitor. There is no separate tower or other computing unit, and that means this computer is space efficient. All you need is a place wide enough to handle the width of the monitor. The keyboard is certainly different from the one I was using previously and it took some adjusting to get used to. But this is the case with any new keyboard and you know what?- the adjustment period for this keyboard was less than a day. In almost no time at all, my wife and I took to the change and had no further issues.

As for the set up, well, it doesn’t get much better than this. I can remember when it would take several hours and much frustration to set up a new computer. But with Acer Aspire, the set up was complete and the computer was ready to use in less than 10 minutes after removing it from the box! We actually scheduled some time in our day, thinking it was going to require a fair amount of time to complete everything. It was so fast I started to worry that I did something wrong. But that wasn’t the case- everything is pretty much ready to go, straight from the package.

Because of our writing and blogging, we often need to have multiple windows open at any given time. This was an issue with my wife’s laptop and it would often slow her computer to a crawl. With this Acer computer, there is no such problem. She can have ten separate windows open, along with Microsoft Word and Excel, and the speed is still as good as ever. Again, this is a definite plus, as computer speed is a top concern for us and many other computer users.

I always try to find something that needs improvement when I write a product review but with the Acer Aspire, I can think of only one thing, and it relates to the Office Suite. They give you Office Suite for a free trial but once the trial is up, you will have to purchase it yourself. Acer could easily make this improvement and while this type of criticism has really nothing to do with the functionality of the product itself, it is about the only issue I can find. Everything else about this computer is well above average.

Computers are essential to my household. We need our computers for writing, for the classes I teach, and other uses. With the Acer Aspire Touch Desktop, we have found a cutting- edge computing machine that fits our needs perfectly and has everything we desire. It’s an excellent computer that would look really good on your desktop and I recommend it when it comes time for your next pc upgrade.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire AIO Touch Desktop, 23.8" Full HD Touch, Intel Core i5-7400T, 12GB DDR4, 1TB HDD, Windows 10 Home, AZ3-715-ACKi5

Kindle Keyboard 3G, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers After running out of space for bookcases and space *on* those bookcases, it was suggested that I look into getting an ebook reader. I decided to give a Kindle a try, and it's made the transition from paper to e-ink a mostly painless transition. The Kindle Keyboard is lightweight - even with a cover it's light enough to hold for long periods of time and usually thinner than most books. It's a little bigger than most paperbacks but smaller than hardcovers, to I can fit it into a larger purse and take it with me if I'll have time to kill during any appointments. Of course, it makes traveling much, *much* easier as now I only need to pack the Kindle and one book to read during that 'power off all electrical devices' time.

The 3G version allows more connectivity but does drain the battery faster. If you want to conserve energy, you can turn it off unless you are downloading a book. The keyboard is small, but I haven't found it too tiny to use when unlocking it for use or searching. My only complaint is sometimes trying to remember when to use the 'Menu' button and the 'square' button for some features - it could be a bit more intuitive (like when to remove a book or sample from the device).

The Kindle Keyboard is only 4GB (actually a little less) and can't be expanded beyond that, but it does hold a lot of books. It's also easy to load books by USB cable and sending via email (to Kindle email account). It's definitely saved at least a bookcase or two! While I would hate to see all books go digital, if you do have an issue with space or you want to have a few books always on hand, a Kindle definitely helps in that regard.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Keyboard 3G, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" E Ink Display - includes Special Offers & Sponsored Screensavers

text_fidelity_a:
Maxell AirStash Expandable Capacity Wireless 8GB Flash Drive 8 A02 (666602) Anyone who doesn't own an iPod or iPad probably won't see the utility of this device. However, for those who know the limitations of a 16GB iDevice, this can come in very handy to extend your storage.

One caveat is that given the cost of the Airstash at the time of writing, if you haven't yet taken the iPlunge, it might be better to go with the 64GB iPad 3 or 2 in the first place. However, if you already own the 16GB, then getting this device becomes an economical option.

The tech specs are covered in the product description, so below are some of my observations based on my experiences using the Airstash with an iPad 2.

Once the Airstash is powered up (by holding down the power button until the green indicator light turns on, then releasing it to see the light flash rapidly three times), you can connect your device to it wirelessly. However, in order to take full advantage of the Airstash, you will need to install the Airstash+ app which you can download from the Apple AppStore for free. This app allows you to access the files that you have copied to the Airstash. Alternatively, you can use a browser and browse to airstash.net for the same functionality.

While it may look like a flash drive on steroids, and works in a similar fashion when you plug it into your computer's USB port, I found it was not as straight-forward a matter when being used to save files. Accessing the files you have placed there is simple enough, but in order to save stuff to it using your iPad/iPod, your app needs to be WebDAV compatible. The Quick Start Guide supplied with the device briefly mentions that once connected you `launch the WebDAV compatible app of your choice'.

Now, if you're like me, then you probably have no idea what this means. What I've discovered is that WebDAV is some kind of `format/protocol' that allows you to save your files to the Airstash. The problem is, not all apps are WebDAV compatible. Apple's Pages, Numbers and Keynote are, but QuickOffice isn't. So if you're a Microsoft Office user like I am, accustomed to QuickOffice, then this device might not be for you. You can read your Office files from the Airstash, but you wouldn't be able to edit them and save them back to the device.

Other observations...

Without installing additional software/apps, mp4 (movie) files on the Airstash played easily on my iPad, but not avi files. (I didn't try digital movies but the product description says that you can play movies loaded on it on your device.)

I couldn't figure out how to save stuff directly onto it that I had downloaded to my iPad, like apps, attachments, books, etc. Maybe there is an easier way, but I had to sync my iPad with my computer first, then copy the files over to the Airstash from the computer.

The iPad could open epub books (in iBooks) and pdf files saved on the Airstash. Presumably there shouldn't be any problems with music and photo files, but I didn't test these either.

It took about 8 minutes to transfer 366MB from my (old) laptop to the Airstash using USB 1.0. With newer computers this should be faster.

Some pros, some cons - consider this is you have an iDevice that needs more storage space.

Amanda Richards April 20, 2012
text_fidelity_b: Maxell AirStash Expandable Capacity Wireless 8GB Flash Drive 8 A02 (666602)

I tested it both as a charging cable and a synching cable with an iPad 2 and it performed flawlessly.

The thing that is the same is this is manufactured to Apple's specs and did earn the MFI certification. Why this is important to me is most third party manufacturers have dropped this legacy cable and are now licensing Apple's Lightning cable (if they are even MFi certified). Decent 30 pin cables are becoming scarce, and the ones from Apple are pricy. That leaves a lot of fly-by-night cables that have a high failure rate, and I am frankly tiring of replacing cables on a monthly basis (I had been purchasing them from a well known big box store as well as a nationwide electronics chain.) When I was offered this one as a review sample I could not resist.

I've been using this as my sole cable for over a week and am not disappointed. The construction is identical to Apple's, and the performance is too. If you are in the same quandary as I - experiencing high failure rates on 30 pin cables - check this one out.

LotFancy Laptop Cooling Pad with 2 LED Fans Ultra Slim Portable Chill Mat for 13 to 15 Inch Computer, Dual USB Ports I received this as a free review sample and it was sorely needed because the internal fan in my ThinkPad T61 finally died. Note: if you are looking at this as a cure know that many laptops report a fan failure then shut down. In the case of mine, I found that I could press the On/Off button briefly when that happened and it would power back up and boot Windows.

This fan array moves a lot of air, promoting excellent heat transfer. So far it has worked well and I have had no premature shutdowns (although I still have to go through the On/Off button sequence every time I power the ThinkPad up.)

Do be aware that this fan array will interfere with other USB peripherals if you power it directly from your laptop, and especially if you add even more peripherals to the ports integrated into this unit. That is because the power draw form USB ports may exceed the capacity of the laptop, especially if you are running it off an unpowered USB hub. I had that problem when I tried running this, a mouse and a speaker from my laptop. I moved this one to a powered hub and the problem was immediately resolved.

Also, this raises a laptop 1 3/8 inches higher at its lowest setting. For me it took a day to become accustomed to the raised typing height, but since it solved a genuine problem the tradeoff was worth it. Just know that you will need to adjust to that and it may slow down your productivity for a day or two.

If your laptop has a fully functioning internal fan this array will augment that and keep your laptop cool even in unairconditioned spaces on a hot day. That will definitely prolong the life of the internal electronics and the hard drive.
text_fidelity_b: LotFancy Laptop Cooling Pad with 2 LED Fans Ultra Slim Portable Chill Mat for 13 to 15 Inch Computer, Dual USB Ports

Because it's mostly pliant plastic
With corner straps made of elastic

If by chance it takes a fall
There's no protection there at all
Without a strap to keep it shut
Your Kindle may just go kaput

In short, this cover's just for looks
To stash your Kindle with your books
A talking point, I will admit
But otherwise, it's just a nostalgic gimmick that's really cute, but not terribly durable*.

*(Not the last line you were expecting)

Amanda Richards, December 27, 2012

text_fidelity_a:
FiiO X5 High Resolution Music Player (2nd Generation)(Titanium) I have used this DAP for about two years now, and I am very pleased with it. It sounds terrific, and I absolutely love the built-in Line-out function for getting the best possible audio into my other devices.
The interface is a little strange and old-fashioned if you’re used to an iPhone. It’s like a weird iPod, but it’s worse. The scroll wheel doesn’t feel nearly as good as the iPod’s, but it’s still a great way to get around in the interface. The interface responds quickly, and has never glitched or frozen on me.
For music navigation, I always use the folder browsing, to browse through the memory cards using my own organization. This is because of two big failures in the built-in browsing:
1. When browsing by genre, you simply get a listing of EVERY track in that Genre alphabetically. So if I select “Classical”, the next screen simply shows me page after page of tracks that start with “1”.
2. When browsing by artist, it uses the actual “Artist” field, instead of “Album Artist”. That’s a little old fashioned now, and most devices are smart enough to use the album artist. It makes it impossible to browse for an album where there are multiple guest artists, but the album itself should all be under one artist.
To do my organization, I have found that JRiver Media Center. That does NOT come with this - you are on your own for software.
I decided on the X5 after looking into the DAC chips Fiio used, and verifying that this could play the formats I was interested - specifically DSD and 24 bit 192KHz PCM. It does both of those with no trouble, and sounds great doing it. Most of my music is in high-resolution FLAC, and CD-resolution Apple Lossless. They both play very well on the X5.
Most of the time, I use mine with a Fiio E12A Mont Blanc Special Edition headphone amp, and Shure SE215 In-Ear monitors. I will also sometimes connect it using the line-out port to my car AUX input or my home stereo. It sounds great in all cases.
I have used it a few times as an external DAC for my Mac, and it works really well at that too - that allows me to connect my headphones through the amp and get some terrific sound.
It has no moving parts, and I can’t imagine that anything on it will break for a very long time thanks to the sturdy aluminum case. If it ever does, I think the only change I would want in my next DAC would be USB-C (the Micro USB connector is just so flimsy on ALL devices, not just this). I don’t need a bigger screen, and I certainly don’t need any more quality.
text_fidelity_b: FiiO X5 High Resolution Music Player (2nd Generation)(Titanium)

PROS: These are super light weight stands that will prop up pretty much any phone or tablet. They are adequate for their purpose. The stand can be adjusted to any position, and the spot that the device rests on is generous. Small, light and easy to carry around these have convenience in portability. Also, as I have the multi pack, you can place them all over or share. Or lose some, haha. Best value is multi pack. Single price is too much for quality of this product.

CONS: They claim anti-skid, but it fails in that feature. So lightweight that if you intend to tap at your device often, depending on what surface you have this placed on, it will scoot around some. I recommend modifying it with a couple beads (or line) of hot glue to give it a rubbery bottom. Or use a scrap of rug pad (that non slip material), or simply use it on a less smooth/hard surface. If just needing to prop up phone or tablet, then it will stay put. The kickstand is solid.

I am most comfortable using it on a smaller device if only because these have barely any weight to them. I have a much heavier stand that I prefer to use, but the price for one is significant. These are basic, light weight and super budget friendly (for multi pack).

Would make for a good stocking stuffer!

So if you're looking to boot fast or upgrade an old spinning mechanical drive, this price is a no brainer.
I don't know how long it will last, as another reviewer said the actual chips used internally aren't bad- they are well known and mass produced. But there's no guarantees as this Fikwot brand hasn't been around long enough to have a reputation for longevity. I'm happily using it to revive an old laptop and turn it into a chromebook. text_fidelity_a:
Belkin N150 Wireless USB Adapter with up to 150Mbps Link Rate We have several networked devices in our house and also several individualized networks configured. Not all of the networks can be seen by all devices so I looked to this Belkin USB WiFi adapter to allow one of the older computer systems to access the most reliable network in the house - a 5GHz network that only one or two of the systems can see.

Installation was a snap. I popped in the CD, told it to install the drivers and we were off to the races. The particular target system was a 32-bit Windows Vista laptop. After just a couple of minutes the driver was completely installed and when I plugged in the USB adapter is was picked up immediately. I could see the desired network as well as several other networks in the neighborhood that were previously invisible to the computer. I shut off the built-in adapter, connected to the 5GHz network and went to the net.

So far, the connection has been very stable and speeds have been excellent. The router to which it is connected is a TP-Link router and so far we have seen no issues between the two devices. I have not had this adapter very long so it is still early to say it’s completely stable but all indicators up to this point have been very favorable.

Several other reviewers have mentioned that this adapter does not work with Linux. This is true - there are no drivers available for this adapter other than for Windows XP/Vista/7/8. If you need an adapter that will allow you to connect a Linux or Mac system to a wireless network, this is not the device you need right now.

So far I can’t find too much about which to complain concerning this router. It seems to be stable and reliable on the system to which it is attached here. I am satisfied with it and based on my experience with it can recommend it - if you’re sticking with Windows.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin N150 Wireless USB Adapter with up to 150Mbps Link Rate

Anker Roav SmartCharge F0 Bluetooth FM Transmitter for Car, Audio Adapter and Receiver, Hands-Free Calling, MP3 Car Charger with 2 USB Ports, PowerIQ, and AUX Output (No Dedicated App) I had no idea something like this existed until I saw it on one of those "Best Things I Ever Bought on Amazon" lists. I had Bluetooth in my old car, and I miss it. My husband's car doesn't have Bluetooth or, at least, it didn't. It does now, and it's so easy to set up! You simply plug this into your car's cigarette lighter, and it automatically finds the radio station that will work the best, depending on your location. You switch over to that station, and boom, connected! You'll even get a man's voice when you turn your car on telling you "waiting for connection," and then "successfully paired" once it syncs up, which doesn't take long at all.

CONS:
You have to leave the car on that radio station all the time for the Bluetooth to work, so this is better if you don't rely on scanning the radio much for car entertainment and use your phone for music more often. You also have to search for a phone number on your phone itself, so it's not ideal for calling people while driving unless you make the phone call first.

PROS:
There are two USB charger ports, so you can charge two phones at the same time (or two devices that use USBs). And here's an added bonus - the charger is turbocharged! I charged my phone from 14% to 65% in a 20-minute trip - excellent! Also, I was listening to an audio book on and off, and every time I turned the car on, the volume remained the same for the audio book - I didn't have to fiddle with it at all.

I didn't even know adding Bluetooth to your car was this easy. I thought I'd have to pay $300 for a mechanic to install it, so I put it off as something I just can't have in my husband's car. But this device makes it an almost seamless experience. The only true caveat I have with it is that I have to load up a phone number to call before I drive, but other than that, you just can't beat this little device for such a low price!
text_fidelity_b: Anker Roav SmartCharge F0 Bluetooth FM Transmitter for Car, Audio Adapter and Receiver, Hands-Free Calling, MP3 Car Charger with 2 USB Ports, PowerIQ, and AUX Output (No Dedicated App)

text_fidelity_a:
HP Stream 7 32GB Windows 8.1 Tablet (Includes Office 365 Personal for One Year) I was really looking forward to trying this tablet out. To date I'd had no exposure to Windows 8.1 or a dedicated Windows tablet. I have had a decent 10.1 inch Android tablet.

First are foremost, the elephant in the room... or rather, the mouse. This is a seven inch wide screen tablet. I have friends whose who online lives are conducted via five inch cell phone screens and they're happy with it. The screen on this tablet is nice. Don't get me wrong. I was able to stream from Amazon video in HD (720) and the video was crisp and clean. Images display well but, again, the screen is just seven inches. I can't imagine trying to be productive with something so small.

For a device with only one gig of RAM this runs Windows fairly well. I wws able to load several Windows programs including the Calibrě eBook manager which took a little longer to convert eBooks between formats but did the job. I also loaded a legacy email and Usenet program that I've been using for a decade or longer. Along with directly installed programs I also downloaded a handful of apps from the very buggy Microsoft app store. The store worked less than 50% of the time while I was trying this tablet out. I at one point had to resort to switching to a local login account and then back to my Hotmail logi. It only took about an hour of reading web forums to find that solution to the Windows app store refusing to work.

Two problems I ran into were the sound which is from a single speaker hidden in a slot on one of the short sides of the tablet. If you want to listen to anything other than the default Window's beeps and tones you'll want to pair this with a blue tooth speaker or headphones. The speaker in this tablet is deplorable. The next problem I had was the tablet runs HOT. I was running a program designed for Windows 98, downloading and reading posts un Usenet and viewing a few posted vacation and astronomy images and I had to stop. The tablet was so hot it was uncomfortable to hold and I worried it might overheat and become damaged.

While I was impressed to see Windows running on a small tablet I was thoroughly unimpressed with Windows 8.1 the tile system is just terrible.

So, it has good video quality on a too small screen with horrible sound and a flaky app store to rely upon, though you can download and install normal Windows programs. I just wasn't that crazy about this tablet. And will definitely be sticking with Android and a much larger screen.
text_fidelity_b: HP Stream 7 32GB Windows 8.1 Tablet (Includes Office 365 Personal for One Year)

text_fidelity_a:
Large Print Backlit Keyboard, Quiet USB Wired Computer Keyboard, Full Size Keyboard with White Illuminated LED Compatible for Windows Desktop, Laptop, PC, Gaming, Black I had a keyboard die when I spilled liquid on it so I grabbed the first one I saw available without looking at the details. When I opened the box and found that this was a backlit keyboard with large print keys, I was intrigued. As an old, retired guy, I spend hours a day at the computer gaming, streaming videos, and staying in touch with a far-flung network of family and friends via social media. This keyboard is particularly nice for the gaming. The white backlight against the black keyboard, as well as the large print keys make it very easy for me to hit the right keys when my eyes are bouncing back and forth between the screen and the keyboard while my hands are handling the both the keyboard and the mouse. This keyboard makes my responses faster and more accurate, which I very much appreciate as an older gamer.

There are those irritating glitches though. One of the worse is that the backspace key constantly sticks. Thankfully, I don't use that key in my gaming, or this keyboard would be totally unusable for me. When typing things like this review though, or posts on social media, that sticky key is very frustrating. Every time I have to backspace to clear a mistake I have to hit that key repeatedly, like I had to do three times while typing this sentence. What makes it even worse is that there is no telling how many hits it takes to move back the necessary amount of spaces. So it is very easy to backspace too far, causing even more mistakes.

Another glitch is that the keys seem bigger than on my last keyboard. I don't notice that in gaming, but when typing more than a few sentences of text, my hands and fingers begin to feel some strain. There are some minor glitches too. The volume control on my speakers is in an awkward place to reach. My last keyboard had separate volume control keys, making it easy to adjust the volume from the keyboard. This one also has volume controls but they are on the function keys, requiring two buttons to be pressed to raise or lower the volume. That sounds like a small thing but every time I adjust the volume,it is a bit irritating to have to hit two keys instead of one. And finally, this keyboard bills itself as "quiet". Hah! It's probably the nosiest, clackity clack typing I've done in a long, long time.

All in all, this keyboard feels like a cheaper knockoff of a higher quality one. For now I'll use this one, because I need it. As soon as I find that higher quality keyboard though, this one is getting tossed out.
text_fidelity_b: Large Print Backlit Keyboard, Quiet USB Wired Computer Keyboard, Full Size Keyboard with White Illuminated LED Compatible for Windows Desktop, Laptop, PC, Gaming, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Linksys AC1900 Wi-Fi Wireless Dual-Band+ Router with Gigabit & USB 3.0 Ports, Smart Wi-Fi App Enabled to Control Your Network from Anywhere (EA6900) When I first set up a home network, I selected a Cisco "Linkys" G router (EA1300) because I recognized the brand name. Later I upgraded to a Cisco dual-band N router ([[ASIN:B007IL7AKM Linksys EA4500]]), which was--and still is--a superb router. My latest upgrade, to this LINKSYS AC1900 (EA6900) DUAL BAND SMART WI-FI ROUTER, represents another leap forward in the performance of my home network.

The wireless signal is stronger in every corner of my two-story condo. All of my devices (some 25 computers, tablets, music players, Kindles, cellphones, Roku, etc.) connect very quickly. Best of all, I'm getting Comcast's promised high-speed Internet speeds of more than 50 Mbps with the Comcast-supplied new telephony modem. (An online speed test site just now clocked the download speed at 57 Mbps). In fact, my present home network is capable of even faster speeds--the home network is limited by the speed of the slower external Comcast network.

This router is extremely easy to set up. You just connect it, and follow the prompts from the built-in software. Whenever you access the router to adjust the settings, and click on some part of the Menu, you find excellent "contextual" help screens that fully explain the meaning of each of the settings. The Menu is set up differently from the menus for the EA4500 and EA1300, but the basic methodology for the settings is the same--the settings are just presented in a way that's easier for a non-techie user to understand.

I read a newspaper review that recommended NOT buying this excellent EA6900 router, because of testers' problems with the second band and with nonfunctioning USB ports. I think that the testers probably received a defective router--and should have requested a replacement. Even a reliable brand like Cisco may sometimes ship an occasional bad electronics device.

Because I only need a single-band router, I haven't tested the second band on my EA6900 router. (The second band did work fine on my EA4500 router, but using the second band didn't improve the signal strength, so I didn't continue using it.) However, I did test the USB ports on the EA6900, and both work really well. In fact, the router recognized and easily accessed a couple of external wireless storage drives--connected with a 100-foot (!) USB cable--when my PC was flakey about recognizing those same drives when they were connected directly to the PC with the long cable.

I absolutely love this EA6900 router, which I've been using for more than a month now. Because of my home wiring, the router is located a long way from any of my wireless devices, and I have a lot of nearby neighbors with competing wireless Internet connections. But with the EA6900, there have been virtually no dropped connections, and the strong signal is something that I've long been wishing for!
text_fidelity_b: Linksys AC1900 Wi-Fi Wireless Dual-Band+ Router with Gigabit & USB 3.0 Ports, Smart Wi-Fi App Enabled to Control Your Network from Anywhere (EA6900)

text_fidelity_a:
Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 (10.1-Inch, Wi-Fi) 2012 Model I thought long and hard about a tablet, knowing that for me it would basically be a toy. Plus I already had a Nook Color. When the iPad2 reduced in price, I thought about getting one of those, but decided against it for the following reasons: (1) no Flash--and yes, I know HTML5 is going to make that obsolete, but in the meantime many websites have a lot of money invested in Flash animation and even restaurants use the silly format to show you their menus (geez, just give us a LIST already--I don't need pretty pictures to find out if you serve something I can eat) and (2) I'm already invested in the Android market and would have to buy many iPad apps that I already have free from Android.

I have not even used it for a week yet, but this a preliminary review with some information I saw requested in other reviews (not necessarily here at Amazon).

UPS delivered this a little before 6:30 p.m. I immediately plugged it into the charger and left it alone. It was charged by 10 p.m. (it might have been earlier, but the unit was away from me and I heard no bleep or flash that might have have indicated the charge was finished). So it does not take six or eight or ten hours to charge as I have seen claimed on other sites. By midnight I was attached to wireless, had gotten into all my accounts and Android apps and was happily surfing and rearranging my home screen.

I used this over the weekend at a science fiction convention. I did not use it constantly, but turned the screen on and off all day for about a 12-hour period, reading Facebook and blogs, checking the news and weather, looking at the convention schedule online, playing short You Tube videos, etc. Nothing excessive, but sometimes did have it on for a half hour to 45-minutes at the time. I also do not have a lot of widgets going, like the Accu-Weather and news widgets that come pre-loaded on the home screen. (They delete easily.) In that 12-hour period it never got below 78% on the battery. It's very quick and fast and responds to a Targus stylus (rubber tipped) wonderfully, much better than my Nook color. The resolution of the screen is impressive. Maybe it's not the new iPad's "retinal display," but it's very, very sharp and bright, even though I keep my brightness turned down to save power. I downloaded the Nook app and the magazines I subscribe to look gorgeous and are simple to read; if not, a tap of the screen makes the text bigger. The unit also comes with Zinio preloaded, an app I plan to use to subscribe to non-US magazines. Kindle books look nice as well, but to me this is too large for marathon reading sessions. I prefer my Nook Color for that. Like my Android phone and my Nook Color, it connects to wireless like a dream, which is more than I can say for my laptop.

Things that might lead you to choose another tablet: (1) The camera is nothing special. It takes good close ups, but further away was problematic. However, I was in a low-light situation each time. Taking photos outside may be totally different. Why Samsung chose to remove the flash I have no idea. Silly, really. But who buys a tablet to take pictures with? (2) With a stylus I can tap to enlarge an image (like Google Maps), but not make it smaller and there is no plus or minus sign on the screen as on my Android phone. (3) Blogger doesn't work in the browser; you have to download the Blogger app, but that works well. iExit doesn't work on it, either. Rats. (4) As at least one other person mentioned, the screen cap button is right in a place where you can hit it easily. I thought of a good use for it this weekend (took a screen cap of the online schedule for the convention I was at, made a short-cut of it to the screen, then pulled up the screen cap for reference rather than going to the web page all the time). Very convenient! (5) Hate the pre-loaded websites in the browser, but I have seen this on other tablets. Apparently we the public are stupid (or lazy) and can't find our own favorite websites and bookmark them. [eyes roll], and (6) my Bluetooth keyboard won't work with it right now because there is as yet no driver for Android 4.0 (Ice Cream Sandwich).

I hope to check back with further comments.

[A few weeks later after I bought this, my husband found an Asus Transformer (TF300) at a good price. It appears to be just as good as this Samsung and the camera is better. It has a zoom and does take a better photo. So if you were looking for a tablet with a better camera the Asus Transformer may be for you. Note: It doesn't have a flash either.]

[Update July 31, 2012 to answer "How long does the battery last"?: I was sick and tired of not seeing any Olympic equestrian coverage except for a couple of hours in the wee hours of the morning, so downloaded the "Live Extra" Olympics app from the Android Market. This carries live streaming of events as well as archived events. This morning I watched about two hours of live streaming of the jumping finals. When that ended I watched six hours of cross-country eventing replay. Then about an hour and forty minutes of the replay of the jumping. I had my brightness at about 35%. This got me down to 10% of the battery from a full charge. Quite satisfactory.]
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 (10.1-Inch, Wi-Fi) 2012 Model

They said it would improve my indoor shots (because the CP 5000 has a terrible flash built-in), but instead it overloads the shots and they come out mostly white.  I read the manual carefully and it looks like the reason is that this flash is built to automatically or manually focus the light for a 14mm to 70mm lense and the CP 5000 has a 7.2mm lense.  I subsequently purchased a Nikon D70s camera (1,000,000 times better camera) and this flash is great for extremely dark shots on that camera (though the built-in flash is perfect for fill so this is really only for night shots and shots in darkness where I want to get something far away).  If you own a CoolPix camera, consider buying a used flash that isn't as powerfull.  If you own a D70s and want superior night photography, this is the best flash in the world (good thing I ended up in the latter end of the spectrum).

text_fidelity_a:
Digital Camera Auto Focus 2.7K 48MP Digital Point and Shoot Camera with 32GB Memory Card,16X Zoom, Time Lapse Vlogging Camera Digital Cameras for 8-15 Years Kids Teenagers Students Boys Girls This is a great little camera. It takes surprisingly good pictures. I guess I wasn't expecting much for a kids camera. It is pretty easy to operate. All the pictures in my review were taken on my recent visit to Colorado. As you can see, it handled a variety of shots with aplomb. The wildflowers was a closeup, the two landscapes were long shots with varying light conditions. The stained glass shot is the ceiling on the Broadmore Hotel in Colorado Springs. Everything came out clear and beautiful. I am not very steady when I hold a camera, so I was pleasantly surprised to find that most of my shots aren't fuzzy or blurred from my wobbly camera holding.

The only reason I didn't give this camera a top rating is because of the viewfinder. There isn't one, and the view screen is stationary. There is no way to rotate it or adjust it so that you can see what you are trying to shoot from any angle that you might hold it at. That made getting a good shot very challenging. The wildflower shot, for instance, was taken completely blind. I could not see the view screen at all. That would have meant crawling on the ground to see the screen. I can't get on the ground (mobility issues). I had to just gold the camera in front of the flowers and snap the picture, hoping for the best. The other issue is that, because you can't adjust the view screen, lighting conditions often make the screen unseeable, even if you are looking straight at it. The second landscape photo (the one on the right) was impossible to see what I was shooting at, even though I was looking directly at the screen. The lighting prevented me from being able to see the screen. Luckily, I got a good shot anyway, but I really don't like shooting blind.

So, overall, I recommend this camera. It is a good beginning camera. Very basic, takes good photos. It's just hard to use in some circumstances.
text_fidelity_b: Digital Camera Auto Focus 2.7K 48MP Digital Point and Shoot Camera with 32GB Memory Card,16X Zoom, Time Lapse Vlogging Camera Digital Cameras for 8-15 Years Kids Teenagers Students Boys Girls

I personally can't handle the noise cancelling aspect, as it hurts my ears and gives me weird head pressure.. so I'm super happy I can turn that off.

My headphones lasted about 3 days, listening about 4-6 hours per day. The headphones only take about 30 minutes to charge as well.
They are suuuuuper comfortable.

I am a smaller person, and a big issue I have with most headphones is they're way too big for my head, so I can't lean my head back onto the bed or couch with them on.
Not with these! I can lean my head back FINALLY, and I barely feel like I'm wearing them.

I had beats before this, and they hurt my ears and my head because they were so weirdly shaped and tight. Like my ears would literally fall asleep. I seriously don't even notice I'm wearing them. No tightness, no pressure, no ears falling asleep.

The case they come with is high quality, and it comes with an aux cord in case you want to listen that way!

The sound cancelling is... Amazing. Literally no sound got through. I thought my husband was messing with me and just mouthing words at me, but no.. he was speaking quite loudly.

Highly, highly recommend. Probably my favorite out of all the ones I've tried.. and I've tried about 7 just this past year.
Splurge and get them, you will not regret it.

text_fidelity_a: SENNHEISER HD 559 Open Back Headphone - Black Unlike the Sennheiser HD 598 headphones I often use, the HD 559 does not include a 3.5mm adapter plug, so if you need one, have it or you will be unhappy should you want to use these for a laptop or other small device.  To test these, I kept my adapter in the laptop and switched between the two headphones, listening to an assortment of various tracks so I could really compare the audio elements and physical feel of the headphones.  I prefer the HD 598 headphones over this newer model and see that they are both comparable prices now because a newer model is available of the 598's.  You may prefer the HD 559's if you prefer a tinner, bass accentuated audio, but I would rather hear the differentiation between the elements of audio which I hear more clearly with the HD 598's.  The separation is simply more refined and I guess I'm spoiled. The newer 559 is cheaper than the upgraded higher end model, and i find them to be a tighter fit which becomes uncomfortable and irritating when worn for hours at a time, something that I never experienced with the others.  I think this band is stiffer, too. These produce a much less elegant sound which some may prefer, but the more I listen to these, the more I wonder if there is something wrong with them due to the pounding sound which is replicated each time I switch to them.  To avoid prejudice, I had an assistant do the switching for me as I kept my eyes closed through several songs and an audio narration.  I worked in the film and video industry and always used Sennheiser earphones, so my experience with the brand spans decades. These just don't match up, and that may just be the cause of my disappointment. They are not bad headphones, they are not great for my desires in experiencing audio in either recording or playback modes.  Of note is that the detachable long cable is nowhere near as easy to remove or insert as my other headphones which is of concern.  This set was made in China and it comes in a no frills 2 part box with a simple document written in numerous languages.
text_fidelity_b: SENNHEISER HD 559 Open Back Headphone - Black
